answer: Each identity binds an enclave that keeps its key inside the chip. A beacon challenges it each epoch; its attestation carries a monotonic counter, so a second identity from one chip reveals reuse. Its opal seal, the attestation hash, is published once, and a prism check of fingerprint, counter, and key binding freezes mismatches and burns the 80-credit bond. The k-th fake needs a k-th device and bond: 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 devices and 80,000 credits. A device farm fails: a reused chip shows one fingerprint and rising counters, clustered and burned. Honest agents pay once.
